oneLine: Tracks who is on shift and on which process path: commits each shift's headcount plan, assigns certified people to paths and flags paths that are short of people.

rows.title: Propose heads for a path
rows.story: A shift lead asks how many people a path needs for a forecast workload. With no planned rate, the measured rate is used. If people on that work are often idle, the answer is trimmed. Nothing is saved.
rows.policy: Whenever no rate is given, use the measured rate; trim the heads when the idle share is high

rows.title: Commit the shift's headcount split
rows.story: A shift lead commits how many people go on each path. A line is refused if its heads exceed the stations installed, the hours the heads can work or the live station count. One announcement goes out per path line.

then.does: turns each plan line into a labour limit for the shift's hours
keeps the latest labour plan per path and checks it against its own plan

rows.title: Start an associate's shift
rows.story: A shift lead puts an associate on the roster with their certifications and, optionally, their site. Starting again for the same associate restarts the roster entry instead of failing.

rows.title: Certify an associate
rows.story: A shift lead adds a certification, such as pick, pack or hazmat, to an associate on shift. A path that needs a certification can only take people who hold it.

rows.title: Start a break
rows.story: A shift lead logs the start of an associate's break. Nobody can be assigned to a path while on a break.

rows.title: End a break
rows.story: A shift lead logs the end of the break, and the associate can be assigned to a path again.

rows.title: Assign an associate to a path
rows.story: A shift lead, or an agent acting for one, puts an associate on a path. They must hold the path's certification and not be on break. Moving someone ends their old assignment, so nobody is on two paths at once.

rows.title: Spot a path that is short of people
rows.story: Asking for a path's staffing gap compares planned heads with people actually assigned. If the path is short, a notice is raised as a flag only. Nobody is moved: a human decides.

rows.title: End an associate's shift
rows.story: A shift lead ends the shift. The associate's active assignment is closed first and its hours are logged against the shift.
rows.policy: Whenever a shift ends, close the associate's active assignment and log its hours

rows.title: Keep the process-path list
rows.story: process-path-management announces every path that is defined, revised or retired. This context keeps its own list, used to check plans and to work out which certification a path needs.
rows.policy: Whenever a path is created, revised or retired, update the local process-path list

rows.title: Keep the measured rates
rows.story: labor-performance reports how long tasks really take and how idle people are. This context keeps the latest figures per task type, so a proposal can use a real rate and the staffing gap can show idle time.
rows.policy: Whenever a task's performance is recorded, update the measured rate and idle share of its task type

rows.title: Feed the labour report
rows.story: The service reads its own announcements and keeps daily labour figures: shifts, breaks, certifications, assignments and understaffing. They feed the labour report.
rows.policy: Whenever a labour or shift event is announced, add it to that day's labour figures

hotspots.text: Committing a shift plan asks fulfillment-execution live for station counts. If that call fails, the whole commit is refused. Moving it to events is a follow-up.
The installed-station count on a commit is supplied by the caller and cannot be verified here, so a second check against the live count was added.
With no planned rate and no measured rate yet for a path, a proposal comes back with zero heads rather than an error.
Messages that cannot be processed go to a holding area with no alerting and no replay tool.

opportunities.text: The live call to fulfillment-execution for station counts, and the REST rollback for measured rates, are tracked as follow-ups to move onto events.
The deprecated buildingId name will be removed only by a later announced breaking decision; siteCode is already the canonical name.
